judge.rationale: The implementation correctly satisfies the functional requirements: it detects added, removed, and changed fields, produces explicit records with field/before/after keys, and sorts by field name. However, it violates the Zen of Python in several ways. The missing_before/missing_after boolean variables add unnecessary indirection when a simple unified comparison would suffice. The three-branch if/elif/elif structure with redundant `.get()` calls (which already return None for missing keys) duplicates logic that could be collapsed into a single, cleaner check: just compare `previous.get(field)` vs `current.get(field)` and emit a record when they differ — this naturally handles all three cases (added, removed, changed) without special-casing. The explicit sentinel booleans make the code longer and harder to audit at a glance without adding clarity. A simpler, flatter implementation would be more Pythonic and easier to verify for correctness.
